description:
A local-first outliner and daily-journal note app (Logseq-style).

Zorite is a cross-platform (macOS + Windows + Linux) local-first
daily-journal and outliner note app. Logseq-style: an infinite-scroll
journal of daily pages plus linked [[wiki-link]] pages, written in
Markdown and stored in a local SQLite database.

Embed and annotate PDFs, drop in images, and search across
everything — no cloud, no account; your notes stay on your machine.
Highlights
Whiteboards grow up: sticky notes, checklists, curved arrows, groups, search,
PNG / SVG export, and Arabic and Hebrew that read right to left. The graph
gets five styles, the app an accent color, All pages your journal days, and the
editor line duplicate / move. Underneath, Zorite moves to GPUI Kit 0.10.
Added
- Accent color. Settings → Appearance → Accent color recolors the
  dates, section labels, links and selections with one of eight swatches or
  any color from a picker, in any theme. Default goes back to the theme's
  own color.
- Journal days in All pages. A new Journal chip lists every day you
  wrote something, newest first, with its first line as a preview. Year and
  month chips narrow it down (#186).
- Graph styles. The graph panel switches between five looks: Classic (the
  graph as it was), Nebula, Islands, Focus and Timeline. Pages are grouped into
  topics from their links, nodes glide between layouts, and your pick is
  remembered. New styles are one file each; see src/ui/graph/style.rs.
  Clicking the panel's title bar retracts it out of the way. Timeline places
  imported pages at their first journal mention instead of the import day.
- Right-click a page in the graph for the same menu pages have everywhere
  else: favorite, open in a new tab or window, copy, export, rename, delete.
- The command palette highlights what you typed in each result.
- Duplicate (⌘D / Ctrl+D) in the editor copies the selection right after
  itself, or with nothing selected, the line the caret is on (a math block,
  table or code block whole) (#199). ⇧⌘D / Ctrl+Shift+D duplicates every
  line the selection touches, and ⌥⇧↑/↓ / Alt+Shift+↑/↓ moves them up or
  down, carrying list items' children and whole blocks like dragging does.
- Whiteboards:
  - Arabic and Hebrew on a board read right to left: Arabic letters join,
    lines mixing them with English order correctly, and the caret, selection
    and checkboxes follow, in exports too. Left / Right move the way they
    point, and a sticky's right-to-left text starts at its right edge.
  - Search finds the words on a board: text boxes and shape labels, with
    the matching line shown under the result.
  - Export a board as PNG or SVG, or copy it as an image, from its
    right-click menu (sidebar, tab, search, All pages). Exports are on white,
    in the board's own font, with images included.
  - Duplicate the selection with ⌘D / Ctrl+D or by Alt-dragging it; arrows
    between copied shapes stay attached to the copies.
  - Group and ungroup with ⌘G / Ctrl+G and ⇧⌘G / Ctrl+Shift+G (or the
    right-click menu). A group selects, moves and copies as one.
  - Sticky notes: the new toolbar tool (key N) drops a paper note with a
    folded corner, in one of five colors, and starts typing from the top-left;
    long text wraps and shrinks to fit.
  - Curved lines and arrows: three curved tools in the Lines menu, and a
    handle in the middle of any selected line or arrow that bends it (drag
    it back onto the line to straighten). Hold Shift while dragging to move
    the curve's peak along the line. With any line tool, drag from a shape
    to draw an arrow attached to it.
  - Ctrl+Home / Ctrl+End (⌘↑ / ⌘↓) jump to the start or end of board
    text while editing it.
  - Bullets and checklists in board text: start a line with * or -
    for a bullet, or [ ] for a checkbox, in a text box, a shape or a sticky
    note. Enter continues the list, and clicking a box ticks it.
  - Typing a shape's label, the caret now moves on Enter and Space right
    away instead of waiting for the next letter.
Fixed
- Linux:
  - Copy as image works on Linux (X11 and Wayland) by handing the PNG to
    wl-copy or xclip; it put empty text on the clipboard before. Without
    the tool, Zorite says which one to install.
  - Board text in fonts without ☐ / ☑ or a script (Arabic, Hebrew,
    Japanese…) draws from a system font that has it, on the board and in
    exports, on distributions that keep fonts outside the usual folders
    (NixOS, Fedora, Arch).
  - Ticking a checklist box works without editing the text first.
  - Enter on a selected shape or text box starts editing it.
  - Undo (Ctrl+Z) takes back an image pasted into a page.
  - Ctrl+Shift+F selects the previous search so typing replaces it.
  - Settings → Mode says Glass is always dark instead of quietly
    ignoring Light.
- Whiteboards, from a test pass on macOS, Windows and Linux:
  - Pasting an image (⌘V / Ctrl+V) onto a board works; it didn't on
    Windows or Linux.
  - Save as template keeps the name you type, in its own "Template name…"
    field; the page-card dialog's field is focused too.
  - The templates gallery, color picker and menus are opaque, so a busy
    board no longer shows through them.
  - Shape labels stay readable on their fill, e.g. a template's pastel
    boxes in a dark theme.
  - Right-click selects the shape under it; on empty canvas it clears the
    selection, and its Paste lands where you clicked.
  - A connector arrow attaches to the connector that lights up when you let
    go near a shape.
  - Esc closes an open toolbar flyout, and with nothing selected puts a
    drawing tool down (back to Select).
  - Double-clicking the toolbar's grip also turns it back into a row.
- Opening a page no longer changes its Updated date. Viewing (or clicking
  into) a page saved it unchanged and stamped it as edited.
- Glass themes stay readable where nothing blurs behind the window (GNOME,
  X11): the glass is thicker there instead of plainly see-through.
- Menu-bar items that open a field (command palette, find, search, new
  page) keep the keyboard on that field, and an opened whiteboard takes the
  keyboard so tool keys work without a click first.
- Nix builds report their real version in Settings → Updates (the flake:
  the newest release plus the commit) instead of v0.1.0 with an update nag.
- A Persian or Arabic page title is right-aligned like its body.
- Closing a find bar with Esc leaves the keyboard on the window, so
  shortcuts work again without a click.
- Deleting a whiteboard closes its open tab.
- Copying text works on Linux X11. The copied text disappeared as soon as
  it was put on the clipboard, so nothing could be pasted, not even back into
  Zorite.
- Esc out of editing keeps the keyboard on the window, so shortcuts work
  right after it.
- Searching with one or two letters is fast again. Short searches also
  scanned whiteboards' canvas data, which on a big board took over a second
  per keystroke.
- All pages keeps its scroll position when you switch tabs and back.
- The PDF page counter shows the last page once it fills the view.
- Timeline keeps the year in view beside the graph panel, and every graph
  style's hint mentions Ctrl/⌘-scroll to zoom.
- Enter in whiteboard text breaks the line on Windows, and Enter and Tab
  add mind-map nodes there again; both were swallowed as if typing in an
  input method (gpui-whiteboard 0.5.6).
- The Edit menu works in journal days and pages, and shows the shortcut
  for every item. Undo, Redo, Cut, Paste and Select All did nothing there
  before.
- Esc out of a menu-bar menu (Windows, Linux) gives the keyboard back to
  what you were typing in, so shortcuts work again without a click.
- Search results preview as plain text, without Markdown markers.
- Greyed-out letters in All pages are easier to read.
- The graph's zoom hint says Ctrl on Windows and Linux, not ⌘.
- Graph labels keep clear of dots and edges in every style, and stay inside
  the window.
- A locked notebook's unlock screen wears your theme (and accent color)
  instead of the default.
- Journal days in All pages preview as plain text, without Markdown
  markers or link brackets.
- The first click in a freshly opened graph lands on the node under it.
- Graph labels sit above their dots, so the pointer no longer covers them,
  and long names no longer pile on top of each other.
- The graph honors your OS's reduce-motion setting: switching styles jumps
  straight to the new layout instead of gliding.
- Journal days can be deleted. Right-click a day in All pages or search results
  → Delete page removes it after a confirmation. The menu offered it
  before, but nothing happened (#186).
- Pressing Enter in whiteboard text adds one line break, not two. Thanks to
  eiei114, whose fork in nottio found and
  fixed it.
- Glass theme over light backgrounds. Greyed-out filters in All pages and
  the highlight under the mouse were hard to see when a white window sat behind
  Zorite; the glass is a little darker and both stand out more.
Changed
- Moved to GPUI Kit 0.10.0 (gpui-pre 0.3.12), in step with Baudrun,
  PortFinder and etch341. The Linux fix for Arabic dots and other combining
  marks (#108) is carried over again.
